corrected_value.authors: Brown, J., Lusch, R. & Nicholson, C. Y.
corrected_value.title: Power and relationship commitment: Their impact on marketing channel member performance.

decisions.location: Section 5.3 (The comparison of the results in the United States and those of Brown et al. (1995)), lines 1252-1274; References, lines 1447-1449
decisions.quote:
We find that the impact of non-mediated power  on normative relationship commitment and 

that  of  mediated  power  on  instrumental  relationship  commitment  in  the  United  States  are 

consistent with the findings of Brown et al. (1995). Moreover, the results show that expert and 

legitimate power are negatively associated with whereas referent power is positively associated 

with  instrumental  relationship  commitment,  which  provides  a  possible  explanation  of  the 

finding  of  the  insignificant  effect  of  non-mediated  power  on  instrumental  relationship 

commitment  (Brown  et  al.,  1995).  The  result  reveals  that  different  bases  of  non-mediated 

power  may  have  conflicting  effects  on  instrumental  relationship  commitment  and  hence 

researchers need to consider the individual effects of different bases of non-mediated power. 

Moreover, we find that reward, coercive and legal legitimate power do not significantly affect 

normative relationship  commitment,  whereas Brown et  al. (1995) find that mediated power 

significantly reduces normative relationship commitment.
decisions.reason: 1. Empirical retesting: Zhang, Zhao, Huo, & Flynn (2022) collect new survey data from United States manufacturers (N = 202) to test the power-relationship commitment hypotheses originally tested in the United States by Brown, Lusch, & Nicholson (1995) (Introduction, lines 115-129, 207-210) and dedicate Section 5.3 (lines 1250-1286) to directly comparing their US empirical findings against Brown et al.'s (1995) findings on mediated/non-mediated power, instrumental/normative commitment, and power-symmetry moderation. Consistent with the Coleman pilot objection, explicit empirical retesting and results comparison in a dedicated results/discussion subsection establishes a genuine replication target rather than mere background. 2. Source-backed identity: The reference list (lines 1447-1449) identifies the work as Brown, J., Lusch, R. & Nicholson, C. Y. (1995), 'Power and relationship commitment: Their impact on marketing channel member performance', Journal of Retailing, 71, 363-392 (no DOI is printed in the primary source). 3. Absence and non-equivalence: The sole shipped row (input_row_index 270, 10.1016/j.jom.2007.08.002) is Zhao, Huo, Flynn, & Yeung (2007/2008) in Journal of Operations Management (represented by sibling target_index 0), a separate study of Chinese manufacturers by a different author team. Report equivalence does not apply. 4. Prior adjudication: Neither prior_adjudication_path nor prior_state_path exists for this work.
